run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T09:16:42Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend is firing because frontend's ad-serving requests fail while its dependency, the ad service, is crash-looping: the ad container in pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 (owned by ReplicaSet ad-554b849958, owned by Deployment ad) was repeatedly killed by the kernel OOM killer (reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137), reaching 4 restarts with container ready=false, and a BackOff event count of 23. The ad Service endpoints object holds only notReadyAddresses, so frontend has no ready ad backend. Frontend's own span metrics show error status concentrated exactly on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, the internal route executing api route (pages) /api/data, the server span GET /api/data (each about 46.8% error ratio at 09:20Z) and tcp.connect (100% error), while frontend's CartService and CheckoutService client spans recorded 0 errors. Frontend's error-span rate turned non-zero at 09:16:00Z and produced the exact value in the alert annotation (2.622222222222222) at 09:20:30Z and 09:24:30Z; ad's own span rate collapsed from about 1.74/s at 09:15:42Z to 0 by 09:21:42Z, and ad recorded no error spans of its own, so it stopped serving rather than returning errors. Deployment ad (1 replica, container memory limit 450Mi) is at generation 1 / revision 1 and its single ReplicaSet was created 08:38:18Z, so no ad rollout is visible in the window; all 5 nodes report MemoryPressure=False and the other 20 otel-demo pods are Ready with 0 restarts, which points to a container-level memory-limit breach in the ad workload rather than node pressure. Recorded ad container memory grew monotonically from 331,190,272 B at 08:50:42Z to 371,867,648 B at 09:16:42Z (peak recorded sample 372,563,968 B, about 355 MiB, still below the 450Mi limit), so the exact instant of the breach fell between cadvisor scrapes and is not captured.

claims.text: Pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 (namespace otel-demo, owner ReplicaSet ad-554b849958) has container ad ready=false, started=false, restartCount=4; its lastState termination is reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 finishedAt 09:17:56Z, and its current state is also terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 09:18:58Z. Pod condition Ready is False with reason ContainersNotReady since 09:18:59Z.

Events for ad-554b849958-l9ft5 inside the window include a Warning BackOff event 'Back-off restarting failed container ad in pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5_otel-demo' at 09:23:35Z with count 23, and Started container ad / Created container ad / Pulled image events at 09:20:27Z with count 6.

Of the 21 pods in namespace otel-demo, only ad-554b849958-l9ft5 is not ready (READY=false, RESTARTS=4, LASTREASON=OOMKilled); all other 20 pods are Ready with 0 restarts, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xfrh6.

Deployment ad in otel-demo runs replicas=1 with container ad image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and resources limits cpu=50m/memory=450Mi, requests cpu=10m/memory=225Mi, so there is a single ad pod behind the ad Service.

The ad Service endpoints object contains only notReadyAddresses pointing at pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 (ip 100.96.2.230, nodeName i-0d81a0f472ebdc704) and no ready address, so the ad Service currently has no ready backend; the ad Service itself is clusterIP 100.71.229.37 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad and port tcp-service 8080.

Frontend span metrics at 09:33:59Z (10m rate) show error-status spans only on: frontend GET 0.1117/s, frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 0.1117/s, frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 0.1117/s, frontend GET /api/data 0.1117/s, frontend tcp.connect 0.0053/s, plus frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' 0.1064/s and frontend-proxy 'ingress' 0.1090/s; frontend's CartService AddItem/GetCart and CheckoutService PlaceOrder error rates are 0.

Per-operation frontend error ratios at 09:20:00Z were grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 0.4684, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 0.4684, GET /api/data 0.4684, tcp.connect 1.0 and GET 0.0483, and 0 for grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, GET /api/cart and the /api/cart route.

Frontend's error-span rate (sum of rate over 2m) was 0 through 09:15:30Z, first became non-zero at 09:16:00Z (1.5667), repeatedly produced the value 2.622222222222222 during the burst (e.g. 09:20:30Z and 09:24:30Z), had its last non-zero sample at 09:26:00Z and read 0 at 09:26:30Z.

Ad's total span rate (5m) was steady at 1.60–1.94/s from 08:51:42Z to 09:15:42Z, then fell to 1.03/s at 09:17:42Z, 0.14/s at 09:19:42Z and 0 from 09:21:42Z, while frontend's total span rate stayed about 42.6–46.3/s over the same period.

Ad container memory working set rose monotonically from 331,190,272 B at 08:50:42Z to 371,867,648 B at 09:16:42Z (roughly 5–6 MB per 2 minutes), then the pod-level series dropped to 53,465,088 B at 09:18:42Z, after which five distinct short-lived container instances appear (one reaching 49,025,024 B, another 183,771,136 B, another 66,813,952 B).

The maximum recorded container_memory_max_usage_bytes and container_memory_usage_bytes for the pre-OOM ad container in 09:03–09:20Z were 372,563,968 B and 372,006,912 B (about 355 MiB), i.e. the recorded peak stayed below the declared 450Mi limit.

Ad's own error-status span rate was 0 for its flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean spans at 09:33:59Z (10m), i.e. ad recorded no error spans of its own while failing.

Deployment ad has generation=1, status.observedGeneration=1, creationTimestamp 2026-11-16T08:38:18Z and annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1; its single ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 also has generation=1, creationTimestamp 2026-11-16T08:38:18Z and owner Deployment ad, so no ad rollout or new ReplicaSet is visible in the authorized window.
All 5 cluster nodes report Ready=True, MemoryPressure=False (KubeletHasSufficientMemory), DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False at query time.

At 09:20:00Z the only services with a non-zero error-status span rate (10m) were frontend 1.8404/s and frontend-proxy 0.9316/s, plus background-level values of 0.00175/s each for fraud-detection, recommendation and ad.

Ad's error-status span rate was 0 for its flagd spans at 09:33:59Z while frontend's error-status rate was 1.8404/s and frontend-proxy's 0.9316/s at 09:20:00Z, showing the error status is carried by frontend (and frontend-proxy) spans, not by ad spans.

Primary causal chain: the ad container exceeded its memory limit and was OOM-killed, entered a restart loop (4 restarts, BackOff count 23, ready=false), the ad Service therefore had no ready endpoint, and the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds calls failed at the transport level (tcp.connect error ratio 1.0, GetAds error ratio 0.468), which propagated to frontend's GET /api/data and its API route span and raised frontend's error rate above 0 — the condition the RequestErrorRate alert reports. The alert started at 09:16:42Z, immediately after frontend's error rate first became non-zero at 09:16:00Z.

The alert annotation's current value 2.622222222222222 is numerically identical to a sample of sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) during the burst, which is consistent with the alert being computed from frontend error spans; the rule definition itself could not be retrieved.

The mechanism that reached the limit is unbounded memory growth in the ad process rather than a traffic surge: ad's working set climbed steadily for at least 26 minutes without a corresponding increase in ad span volume. Profiling inside the ad container would be needed to name the growing structure; this evidence set cannot confirm it.

An alternative framing of the same fault is that the ad container's 450Mi memory limit is undersized for the ad service's normal working set, since a steady-state working set of about 355 MiB was observed against a 225Mi request, so the kill may reflect a limit set too close to normal usage rather than only runaway growth; under this framing raising the limit and investigating growth are both needed.

frontend-proxy's own error spans on 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' (0.106–0.109/s) are most likely frontend's failing responses recorded by the proxy: the magnitudes match frontend's error-span rate and the span names place the proxy on the request path to frontend. This is inferred from span names and metric timing only — no trace with parent-child references was available to confirm the edge.

Node-level memory pressure or eviction as the cause is not supported: all 5 nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure=False, and the other 20 otel-demo pods — including frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xfrh6, which a pod listing showed on the same node i-0d81a0f472ebdc704 as the ad pod — are Ready with 0 restarts. node_memory_* series returned no data, so actual node free memory during the burst is unknown and was not used.

A traffic surge into the ad service as the trigger is not supported: ad's span rate was flat at 1.60–1.94/s for the 24 minutes before it collapsed, and frontend's total span rate stayed about 43–46/s, so no increase preceded the OOM.

An ad Deployment rollout or controller-driven pod replacement during the incident window is not supported: Deployment ad is at generation 1 / revision 1, its only ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 has generation 1 and was created 08:38:18Z, the pod keeps the same ReplicaSet owner, and the only ad pod events in the window are Pulled/Created/Started and BackOff. Change history is not integrated, so a change made before 08:38:18Z cannot be excluded.

The ad service returned no errors of its own: its error-status span rate was 0 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and ResolveBoolean while its total span rate fell to 0. This weighs against 'ad is returning application errors to frontend' and instead shows ad stopped serving, so the frontend failures are dependency-unavailability failures rather than error responses from ad.

The recorded ad container peak (372,563,968 B, about 355 MiB) stayed below the configured 450Mi limit, so no sample shows the container actually at 450Mi; the limit breach that the OOMKill proves happened between cadvisor scrapes and the exact value held at the kill is not captured by any sample in this evidence set.

Whether the frontend recovered before the window ended is unverified: the frontend 2m error-span rate reads 0 from 09:26:30Z and frontend's total span rate falls to 0 by 09:29:42Z, while the ad pod is still ready=false in BackOff — the trace-derived series stop producing values, which looks like end of metric ingestion rather than a demonstrated recovery.

Treat the ad workload as the dependency to fix: raise the ad container memory limit (currently 450Mi) above its observed steady-state working set and/or fix the ad memory growth, and run more than one ad replica or a PodDisruptionBudget so that a single OOM-killed pod does not empty the ad Service endpoints.

Add leading indicators: a memory alert on the ad container comparing container_memory_working_set_bytes with its limit, and an alert on ad Service ready endpoints, so these fire before a frontend-level error-rate alert; and have the frontend degrade gracefully when grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds has no ready backend instead of returning errors on /api/data.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule definition could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules (status no_data) both with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert, so the exact expression, threshold and evaluation window behind the reported 'current: 2.622222222222222' are unconfirmed; the value's identity with the frontend error-span 2m rate is a numeric match, not a verified rule.

Jaeger returned no traces for the incident window: traces_search for frontend (09:16–09:24Z and 09:24–09:33:59Z) and for ad (09:16–09:33:59Z), and traces_search_by_tags with error=true for both services, all returned 0 traces and 0 spans (status no_data). No trace_id, span_id or parent reference was available, so the frontend→ad and frontend-proxy→frontend edges are inferred from operation names and metric timing, not from trace parent references.

Node memory series (node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes) returned no data (status no_data), so actual node free memory during the ad container's final minutes is unknown; the node-pressure rejection rests on node conditions at query time and on sibling pods being healthy.

container_spec_memory_limit_bytes, kube_pod_container_resource_limits, kube_pod_container_status_* and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready series are absent from this target (queries returned no_data), so the cgroup limit enforced at runtime could not be compared with the 450Mi value declared in the Deployment, and no restart or OOM counter history is available from metrics.

The exact instant the ad container breached its limit falls between cadvisor samples: the last recorded working set at 09:16:42Z and the recorded peak (372,563,968 B) are both below 450Mi, so how much memory the process actually held at the kill is unknown.

Frontend application logs could not be used: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx returned 0 lines and 0 bytes for 09:14–09:22Z, both unfiltered and with an error/AdService filter (status no_data), so there is no frontend-side log confirmation of the ad connection failures.

Ad log coverage is partial: the previous container instance's logs were unavailable ('previous terminated container ad ... not found'), and the current instance read covered only 09:14:07–09:14:47Z (2678 lines, newest 60 shown, incomplete) — before the first crash — so no panic or OOM log line and no last words before termination are available.

The change_history integration is not integrated, so whether the ad image, memory limit or code changed before the window cannot be checked; the Deployment's generation=1/revision=1 only shows no template change since 08:38:18Z. It is also unexplained why all 21 otel-demo pods share start times of 08:38:18–08:38:20Z.

State after about 09:26Z is unknown: trace-derived series end at 09:26:30–09:29:42Z while the ad pod is still unready, so whether the frontend error rate actually cleared before the window end cannot be stated.
querying http_* and rpc_* metric names also returned no data, so there are no RED-style HTTP or gRPC server metrics to cross-check the trace-derived span metrics for either frontend or ad.
next_steps: Inspect the ad container's memory behaviour and runtime memory configuration for ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad to determine what grows ~5–6 MB per 2 minutes, and check whether the flagd client or OTLP log/metric exporters are buffering.

Decide between raising the ad container memory limit above 450Mi and fixing the growth, then run ad with more than one replica plus a PodDisruptionBudget so one OOM-killed pod does not leave the ad Service with zero ready endpoints.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule from the alerting stack that produced the Alertmanager notification (it is not loaded in the queried Prometheus) to confirm the expression and threshold before tuning it.
Re-collect frontend container logs at the time of a recurrence, since the frontend log stream returned no lines for this incident window.
Review unready-endpoint handling in the frontend so /api/data degrades instead of returning errors when grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds has no ready backend.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | select(.metadata.name|startswith("ad")) | {name:.metadata.name, created:.metadata.creationTimestamp, generation:.metadata.generation, observedGeneration:.status.observedGeneration, updatedReplicas:.status.updatedReplicas, replicas:.status.replicas, owner:.metadata.ownerReferences}

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
